messages.subject: Establishing influence of fixed effects
parts:
Dear INLA community,

I want to establish whether the fixed effects in the model are influential, i.e. whether two levels of the categorical predictor do not overlap with each other. I could think of three different ways of going about it, and I wanted to know if one of these is better and should be preferred and if they are conceptually different from each other. Below I am providing the code with the simulated model and three approaches.

#loading libraries and running the model
library(INLA)
library(dplyr)
library(tidiverse)

set.seed(123)
data <- data.frame(y = rnorm(100, 0, 1)) %>%
  mutate(x = case_when(y<quantile(y,0.5)~sample(c("a","b"),n(), replace = TRUE, p=c(0.85, 0.15)),
                       TRUE~sample(c("a","b"), n(), replace = TRUE, p=c(0.15, 0.85))))

m1 <- inla(y ~ -1 + x, data = data,
           control.compute = list(config = TRUE))

#Approach 1: obtaining differences between two levels from additionally computing posteriors.

m1_post_samples <- inla.posterior.sample(100, m1)

contrast <- inla.posterior.sample.eval(function(...)
{c(xa - xb)},
m1_post_samples)

contrast <- contrast %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  t()

difference_post <- c(quantile(contrast, 0.025), quantile(contrast, 0.975))

#Approach 2: computing linear combinations (the difference between two levels) and checking whether it crosses zero

lc <- inla.make.lincomb(xa = 1, xb = -1)
m2 <- inla(y ~ -1 + x, data = data, lincomb = lc)

difference_lc <- c(m2$summary.lincomb.derived$`0.025quant`, m2$summary.lincomb.derived$`0.975quant`)

#the difference does not overlap with zero
difference_lc

#Approach 3. Visually checking whether the quantiles of two levels overlap (without additionally computing contrasts)

effects <- data.frame(matrix(ncol = 2, nrow = 6)) %>%
  mutate(effects = rep(c("a", "b"), each=3),
    value = c(m1$summary.fixed[1,]$`0.025quant`,
                   m1$summary.fixed[1,]$`0.5quant`,
                   m1$summary.fixed[1,]$`0.975quant`,
                   m1$summary.fixed[2,]$`0.025quant`,
                   m1$summary.fixed[2,]$`0.5quant`,
                   m1$summary.fixed[2,]$`0.975quant`))

ggplot(effects,
       aes(x = value,
           y = effects,
           colour = effects)) +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(w = 0.9), size = 1)

Thank you very much in advance.

Best,
Alyona
